fix(recall): normalize hierarchical tag prefix filters (#266)
commits.body:
Prefix filters now normalize slash and colon separators consistently
across graph, vector and postfilter paths. Legacy graph nodes use
hierarchy-aware fallback rather than string-prefix matching. Exact
matching retains separator distinctions. Documented backfill covers
existing Qdrant payloads without tag_prefixes.

commits.headline: fix(api): validate memory types and expose reliable diagnostics (#268)
commits.body:
Admin preflight permits both supported admin headers while preserving
origin/auth checks. Registered POST/PATCH/batch routes normalize known
memory types, preserve custom strings with a warning, and reject
blank/null/non-string types before mutation. Entity audit validation
returns standard 400 responses. Structured logging emits extras safely
and removes recall query text from structured events, Werkzeug access
logs and vector-search DEBUG logs without mutating shared LogRecords.

commits.headline: fix(enrichment): preserve concurrent memory updates (#269)
commits.body:
Background and JIT enrichment could overwrite newer caller tags and
metadata after PATCH. Enrichment now merges derived additions into the
latest source snapshot; background relationships, derived graph fields
and completion commit in one guarded graph query. Content and timestamp
changes invalidate an obsolete plan, missing planned neighbors preserve
the source row, and per-memory evidence accounting keeps retries from
inflating temporal/pattern counters. Conditional Qdrant tag updates and
nest

commits.headline: fix(embedding): retry failures and preserve vector payload state (#265)
commits.body:
Async embedding jobs now retry bounded provider and Qdrant failures,
reuse vectors only while their source text remains current, and expose
failure/exhaustion counters in `/health.embedding`. The worker waits for
Qdrant application and revalidates graph content afterward so a
concurrent PATCH triggers regeneration. All seven vector writers share a
payload builder preserving temporal bounds, archive state, relevance,
metadata and hierarchical tag prefixes. Explicit placeholder providers
continue

commits.headline: fix(recovery): preserve existing graph data during Qdrant salvage (#263)
commits.body:
Qdrant recovery previously deleted the graph before fetching its source
and could report success after incomplete restoration. Recovery now
validates the complete source, inserts missing memories with original
IDs and API-compatible properties, preserves existing nodes and
relationships, and fails clearly on incomplete recovery. The monitor
avoids graph salvage for a vector deficit and honors CLI > environment >
defaults, including zero.

commits.headline: fix(mcp-sse): preserve active legacy SSE sessions (#262)
commits.body:
Legacy SSE sessions were missing access timestamps, so the
abandoned-session sweep closed every connection within five minutes.
Track activity and keep connected streams alive while cleaning up closed
sessions.

commits.headline: fix(runtime): preserve retries and honor Qdrant safety settings (#264)
commits.body:
Strict Qdrant dimension mismatches now propagate through real collection
initialization and stop default startup. Enrichment retries atomically
transfer inflight protection to a pending retry, preserving bounded
attempt counts and queue completion accounting. Consolidation uses the
configured collection for all seven vector operations and warns on
failed mutations.

commits.headline: Remove stale skills
docs(deploy): Confirm again replays only within the bridge's 7 days
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): the replay promise names the bridge's 7 days
commits.body:
After a confirm that may have paid, the message said confirming the same
Mark paid again replays the first payout, with no limit. The bridge keeps
that record for 7 days, so after that the same confirm could pay again. The
message now says within 7 days of the first try, and after that to check
AffiliateWP first.

commits.headline: fix(payouts): Refresh from live runs the guarded affiliates sync
commits.body:
In local dev the payout page's Refresh from live ran the bare edd sync
(scripts/sync.sh, the full pull). That does nothing for affiliates when
the config leaves SYNC_AFFILIATEWP off, and exits 0 after an affiliate
query fails, so the page reloaded stale data as if it were refreshed.

commits.headline: fix(payouts): keep a row with typed text listed after it leaves the run
commits.body:
A row with no entry in the run that held an unsaved draft vanished when
a republish removed the affiliate from the queue: nothing in the run
kept the row, so the field and its text went with it.

commits.headline: fix(payouts): a first note save keeps the default a reload brought
commits.body:
On a row with no entry, a draft's first save sent the status the row
showed when typing started. If someone put the affiliate's review on
hold meanwhile, the refetched row showed hold (the derived default),
but leaving the note field created a pending entry, overriding the hold
the person could see.

commits.headline: fix(bridge): Mark paid shows only when a real bridge has its signing key
commits.body:
/me offered Mark paid with an https BRIDGE_URL and no BRIDGE_SIGNING_KEY,
though every dry run and confirm would then be refused before it went out.
A real bridge now also needs a nonblank signing key to count as configured;
the staging stub is unchanged.

commits.headline: fix(bridge): a real BRIDGE_URL must be https
commits.body:
A plaintext http origin that answered 200 would carry the signed payout
request and trust its answer, so a made-up payout id could be saved as
paid. A real BRIDGE_URL must now be https (http only to localhost) or the
call is BridgeUnavailable before anything is signed, and Mark paid is not
offered; the staging stub stays the one exception.

commits.headline: docs(deploy): stop when the affiliates-only sync fails, never publish past it
commits.body:
The runbook still said a failed affiliates-review query left the sync at
exit 0 and the queue publishable. The affiliates-only sync now exits 1 and
says not to publish, so the step says to stop, fix the database, and sync
again until it is clean.

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): Mark paid keeps in_progress confirms, stops at auth refusals, names unrecorded referrals
commits.body:
Three ways the flow misread an answer to a confirm. They share the routing in
afterConfirmFailure and its tests, so they land together.

commits.headline: fix(sync): an empty AffiliateWP result replaces the last copy
commits.body:
A query that ran and matched nothing kept the last good JSON. For the
payout queue or the review list an empty answer is the news (the last
unpaid referral was paid), and keeping the old rows would publish paid
balances into the next run. Affiliates endpoints now write the empty list;
every other endpoint keeps its last copy, as before, and a missing TSV
(a concurrent sync) still keeps it for all.

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): a payout that left referrals unpaid is never saved as paid
commits.body:
The bridge core now answers { error: referrals_not_updated, payout_id,
referral_ids } when AffiliateWP recorded a payout but left referrals unpaid.
bridgeAnswer took any result with a positive payout id as a completed payout,
so both routes would have saved the entry paid while those referrals stayed
payable.

commits.headline: fix(bridge): a payout that left referrals unpaid is not reported as paid
commits.body:
AffiliateWP's payouts->add() can insert the payout, fail to mark a referral
paid (a transient database error it does not report) and still return the new
payout id. The core took every positive id as a completed payout, so the
idempotency record kept a success and the Worker marked the entry paid while
that referral stayed unpaid, and payable again next month.

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): a stored review goes on the drawer's snapshot too
commits.body:
A drawer kept open on the row it opened on (the affiliate left the queue)
is never refreshed by a reload, so after a save the form went back to the
old review, and after a conflict every retry went at the old version. The
review the host stored, or the one a conflict showed, now goes on that
snapshot as well (withStoredReview).

commits.headline: fix(workspace): a file import reloads the Partners board too
commits.body:
The import wrote Partners deals through the workspace API but only reloaded
the workspace queries; the board is its own query, so a Partners page kept
the old deals and its next edit went out at a version the import had moved
on. The banner now reloads the board as well. The board's query key lives in
src/shared/partners-pipeline.js so the banner can use it without the save
hook's dependencies.

commits.headline: fix(sync): an endpoint name that matches no query exits 2
commits.body:
./scripts/sync.sh --affiliates affiliates-reveiw skipped every query and
reported a successful sync, so the publish that follows would send the old
files as if refreshed. With an endpoint name that matches no query the script
now says so and exits 2, in any mode.

commits.headline: test(affiliates): pin the cautious amount_changed message on the host
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): amount_changed never sends anyone straight to a fresh payout
commits.body:
On a retry whose replay record was lost, amount_changed means the first
confirm paid, and the server cannot tell that from a first confirm. Its
message said to check again and pay the new figure, which could pay newer
referrals while the first payout stayed unrecorded. It now says this request
paid nothing, an earlier confirm with no answer may have, and to check
AffiliateWP before checking again.

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): import rowForKey in the payout queue
commits.body:
recordedPaid looks the row up with rowForKey, which a merge left unimported,
so every Record as paid that the host stored threw a ReferenceError before
the dialog closed and the run reloaded. A test now checks that every helper
the queue calls is imported, since the render cannot reach those handlers.

commits.headline: fix(sync): --affiliates exits 1 when any query failed
commits.body:
A failed AffiliateWP query left its last good JSON (or none) and the run
still printed Sync complete with exit 0, so the publish that follows could
send a stale queue or a missing review file. The script now counts failed
queries, a failed TSV to JSON conversion included, and names them. With
--affiliates it exits 1 and says not to publish; a full sync still exits 0,
as the dev Refresh button reads it.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): a file that held entries finishes even when nothing was left to write
commits.body:
A real export whose Partners deals were all untouched seed copies, or whose
notes the host already held, wrote nothing, so the file flag stayed unset
and Import a file came back on every page load. A file finishes now when it
wrote, or when it held entries (exportHolds) and none could not be read. An
empty or unreadable file still leaves the button up (R22).

commits.headline: test(dev): the injected-spawn sync test clears the runner flags too
commits.body:
The spawn guard now also refuses on a test runner flag, so the test that
clears the guard's env keys to run an injected spawn clears the process's
runner flags for its duration as well, and a new test pins that a runner
flag alone refuses runSync.

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): a Mark paid retry expires with the bridge's 7 day idempotency window
commits.body:
A kept retry carried no time, so one restored after the bridge had forgotten
its idempotency key (wpf_dash_idempotent keeps it for 7 days) still offered
Confirm again and promised a replay, when that confirm would pay again.

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): one write at a time on a payout row, Mark paid included
commits.body:
At the retry step nothing locked the row: Confirm again could pay while a hold
or a note was being saved. Turning the buttons off on render does not close
that, because a textarea's blur starts its save before the click that follows
it is handled, and before React re-renders the row with Confirm again off.

commits.headline: fix(payouts): keep the review drawer and Record as paid open when their row leaves
commits.body:
The review drawer and the Record as paid dialog looked their row up in
the run's rows on every render. An affiliate with no entry in the run
who fell out of the published queue while one was open (paid outside
the dashboard, then a refetch on focus or reconnect) made the lookup
return null, which unmounted it and discarded an unsaved review or the
typed payment fields.

commits.headline: docs(deploy): the bridge keeps idempotency records as options, not transients
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(dev): the SSH spawn guard also reads the test runner flags
commits.body:
Run by hand as node --test --test-isolation=none, the test files share the
runner's process, so neither NODE_TEST_CONTEXT nor WPF_NO_SPAWN is set and
the guard let the default runners reach production over SSH. It now also
refuses when this process carries a test runner flag (--test, --test-...,
--experimental-test-...).

commits.headline: fix(exec): a conflict drops only the drafts it carries
commits.body:
A field whose save failed with a network error or a 500 kept its sent
marker, and a later conflict on another field dropped it too, losing the
typed text the conflict did not carry. A conflict now drops a draft only
when its value (the conflict's draft) carries that same text; any other
draft stays as an ordinary one with its marker gone. The MRR decision is
saved as a plain string, so it maps its conflict's value back to a field.

commits.headline: fix(exec): a conflict drops only the drafts it carries
commits.body:
A field whose save failed with a network error or a 500 kept its sent
marker, and a later conflict on another field dropped it too, losing the
typed text the conflict did not carry. A conflict now drops a draft only
when its value (the conflict's draft) carries that same text; any other

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): a step that knows no payout warns when its row is recorded paid by hand
commits.body:
A Mark paid step that knows no AffiliateWP payout id (a retry whose first
confirm got no answer, or a may-have-paid failure) was dropped whenever its row
loaded paid. When the Worker saved a Mark paid that is right: normally it is
this very confirm. But when someone recorded the row paid by hand, the confirm
that got no answer may also have paid, and that warning went away with the
step.

commits.headline: fix(partners): a landed deal save goes on the board at its version before the reload
commits.body:
A save's onSuccess returned invalidateQueries, which swallows a failed
refetch. After a network blip, or offline, a save that had landed left
the board showing the old version number. The next save on that deal
went out at that version and came back as a 409 the person caused
themselves.

commits.headline: feat(payouts): show a run's affiliates outside today's queue, and what it paid
commits.body:
With b2, a run lists every entry it holds: queue rows (in_queue: true)
and one row per entry whose affiliate has left the queue (in_queue:
false, every queue column null). The page read every row as a queue
row, so a past month showed today's balances, and a row outside the
queue would have shown a dash for its name, $0.00 due and "()" for its
status.

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): Record as paid from a step that knows its payout starts with it
commits.body:
A Mark paid retry that knows the AffiliateWP payout its confirm made (#501,
named by payout_not_saved) offers Record as paid as the way to save it, but
the dialog opened empty: the person had to find the payout id and the amount
again, and could record the entry paid with no payout id without a word.

commits.headline: fix(partners): Use theirs shows their deal from the refusal, and keeps the conflict when it cannot
commits.body:
"Use theirs" awaited invalidateQueries, which swallows a failed refetch,
and then reset the mutation and remounted the drawer anyway. After a
network blip the cached board still held the person's stale copy, the
conflict and its reapply payload were gone, and the page showed no
error because it hides query errors while cached data exists.

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): a row at the Mark paid confirm step takes no other write
commits.body:
Once the dry run reached the confirm step, the row's status select, hold
reason, note and Record as paid were live next to Confirm, so a hold or a
recorded payment could race the payout AffiliateWP was about to make. Only
checking and paying locked the select and Record as paid; the text fields
locked only while saving.

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): a retry that knows its payout survives its row being paid another way
commits.body:
A kept Mark paid retry that knows the AffiliateWP payout its first confirm made
(payout_not_saved named #501) was hidden, and its kept step deleted, as soon as
its row loaded paid, whatever payout the row was saved with. If someone recorded
the row paid with #77, or with no payout id, the only sign that AffiliateWP
also held #501 went away.

commits.headline: feat(payouts): a run lists every entry it holds, not only today's queue
commits.body:
mergeQueueWithRun built a run's rows from today's unpaid queue alone.
An affiliate paid in a past run has usually left that queue, so an
imported or closed month showed few of the people it paid, and an
affiliate who dropped out on a republish took their row (and anything
open on it) with them.

commits.headline: fix(exec): an Action Plan undo entry leaves the stack only once its undo is stored
commits.body:
Undo last, Undo last 2 and Restore took their entries off the stack at the
click, before the save went out. When that save failed (a network error or
a 500) the store put the task back to completed, but the entry was gone, so
the Undo controls disappeared and the undo could not be tried again. A 409
lost the entry the same way, whichever way the conflict was settled.

commits.headline: fix(exec): an Action Plan undo entry leaves the stack only once its undo is stored
commits.body:
Undo last, Undo last 2 and Restore took their entries off the stack at the

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): the review drawer lists payouts recorded on the host
commits.body:
The drawer's payout history read only AffiliateWP's recent_payouts from
the published review snapshot. Record as paid without an AffiliateWP
payout id never reaches AffiliateWP, so that payout was missing and a
reviewer saw an incomplete payment history.

commits.headline: fix(enrichment): guard temporal plans with source timestamps
commits.body: Reject a background enrichment plan if the source timestamp changes during planning, and compare that timestamp again in the atomic graph commit. Keep newer caller timestamps without installing obsolete temporal relationships.

commits.headline: feat(payouts): local review history returns the affiliate's paid entries
commits.body:
The host's review history now answers paid_entries alongside history, so
the review drawer can list payouts recorded only on the host. Local dev
answered history alone, so the drawer would show less offline than on
the host.

commits.headline: feat(payouts): review history returns the affiliate's paid entries
commits.body:
The review drawer's payout history read only AffiliateWP's recent_payouts
from the published review snapshot. A payout recorded on the host without
an AffiliateWP payout id lives only in payout_entries, so it never showed
there, and the spec asks for host runs alongside recent_payouts.

commits.headline: fix(enrichment): commit planned graph effects atomically
commits.body: Compile the explicit relationship write plan into the source compare-and-set query before derived graph fields and completion are installed. Preserve the source row through optional missing neighbors and namespace helper parameters to avoid collisions.

commits.headline: fix(enrichment): defer effects until source validation succeeds
commits.body: Plan explicit relationship writes before the source CAS, apply them with per-write content guards only after CAS success, and mark completion after effects finish. Count temporal and pattern evidence once per memory so partial-write retries and forced replay cannot inflate observations.

commits.headline: fix(payouts): a draft's first save sends the status it started from
commits.body:
A first save (version 0) creates the entry, so entryPatch also sends a
payout_status, and it took the status the row shows now. When someone
typed a hold reason or note on a row with no entry and, before they left
the field, someone else recorded or marked that row paid, the body said
payout_status: paid. The host answers that with 400 use_mark_paid, which
is not a conflict, so the field kept the text under a misleading error.

commits.headline: fix(embedding): revalidate source after Qdrant applies writes
fix(policy): align live repository agent guidance
fix(affiliates): Record as paid off the table opens at the entry's current version
commits.body:
A Mark paid step whose affiliate has left the queue offers Record as paid built
from its confirm body, at the body's version. After a retry refused with
stale_write or not_approved, that version is the one the refusal said was old,
so Record as paid was refused as stale too. RecordPaidDialog then reloaded,
but with no row in the queue nothing newer came back, and every further try
was refused the same way.

commits.headline: fix(payouts): keep typed payout text through background refetches
commits.body:
The PayPal note textarea was keyed by the run version. With an
unblurred draft, a refetch on focus or reconnect that brought another
editor's note remounted it with the stored note and discarded the
draft before the version-checked save or the conflict handling could
keep it.

commits.headline: fix(partners): one lock for every deal save action, Use theirs included
commits.body:
"Use theirs" awaited the board reload without holding any lock, so both
conflict buttons stayed live. A "Reapply mine" in that window sent the
refused change while dismiss was still running; dismiss then reset the
mutation and remounted the drawer while that change could still land.
"Use theirs" right after a reapply had started did the same.

commits.headline: fix(payouts): sync-wp reads how an entry was paid like everywhere else
commits.body:
sync-wp checked the raw fields of each stored entry. A paid entry an
older server saved with neither paid_via nor wp_synced_at reads as
recorded everywhere else (paidViaOf, entryView), meaning it was paid
outside the dashboard, but sync-wp saw paid_via undefined and sent it to
markPaid. A bulk sync on an existing store could then create an
AffiliateWP payout for the affiliate's current unpaid referrals.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): keep Import a file up when the file had an entry that could not be read
commits.body:
A file holding one valid entry and one the key rules refused (a Partners
deal whose id fails them, say) wrote the valid one and came back done,
since only failed puts counted. runWorkspaceImport then set the file flag
because something was written, so the banner said some entries could not be
read and took the Import button away: after fixing the export there was no
way to bring the corrected entry in short of clearing localStorage.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): keep Import a file up when the file had an entry that could not be read
commits.body:
A file holding one valid entry and one the key rules refused (a Partners
deal whose id fails them, say) wrote the valid one and came back done,
since only failed puts counted. runWorkspaceImport then set the file flag
because something was written, so the banner said some entries could not be
read and took the Import button away: after fixing the export there was no
way to bring the corrected entry in short of clearing localStorage.

commits.headline: fix(policy): distinguish corrections and enforce bare tag namespaces
fix(enrichment): transfer retry guards atomically
commits.body: Keep inflight protection until retry enqueue acquires the state lock, then transition to pending without allowing an ordinary enqueue to reset the attempt counter. Preserve the existing callback signature and queue completion accounting.

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): a refused Mark paid retry keeps its payout id and body
commits.body:
A first confirm answered payout_not_saved leaves a retry step holding the
AffiliateWP payout id and the original confirm body. When that retry was then
refused with stale_write or not_approved, afterRetryFailure replaced it with a
may-have-paid failure carrying neither: the row stopped naming the payout
AffiliateWP had recorded, and once the affiliate left the queue
markPaidOffTable had no body to build its Record as paid action from.

commits.headline: test(logging): isolate recall helper dependencies
fix(exec): an Action Plan undo entry exists only for a completion the host stored
commits.body:
The undo entry was pushed when the task was clicked, before the save went
out. A save that failed, or lost a conflict the person settled with "Use
theirs", left an entry for a completion that was never stored, and a later
"Undo last" wrote its stale previous status over the shared value. The
version check did not stop that: once this browser had loaded the other
person's change, the undo went out at their version and succeeded.

commits.headline: fix(exec): an Action Plan undo entry exists only for a completion the host stored
commits.body:

version check did not stop that: once this browser had loaded the other

commits.headline: fix(logging): redact request queries from access and debug logs
fix(embedding): refresh cached vectors when memory content changes
fix(policy): cover session hooks and legacy OpenClaw guidance
fix(enrichment): preserve concurrent caller updates
commits.body: Rebase derived tags and metadata onto a fresh memory snapshot and commit with an atomic graph comparison. Discard content-stale extraction, preserve caller summaries, and restrict Qdrant synchronization to guarded tags and derived nested metadata keys.

commits.headline: fix(api): validate memory types and expose reliable diagnostics
fix(recovery): accept unset relevance from normal vector payloads
fix(test): require real service integration execution
fix(affiliates): the import never leaves out an entry for a field that does not fit
commits.body:
An entry whose hold reason or ops note was past 20,000 characters, or whose
payout id was not a whole number, was skipped whole, so a paid entry would
show as unpaid on the host and a hold as not held. The entry now comes in
with that field at its default, counted as <run>:<affiliate>:<field>. Only
an entry's affiliate id or status can leave it out.

commits.headline: fix(policy): align companion memory storage examples
fix(embedding): retry failed jobs and preserve vector payload state
fix(mcp-sse): align tag and metadata tool descriptions
fix(recall): normalize hierarchical prefix tag filters
fix(mcp): align tag and metadata tool descriptions with API behavior
fix(runtime): preserve retries and honor Qdrant safety settings
commits.body: Propagate strict vector dimension errors through collection initialization, retry enrichment after inflight cleanup, and use the configured Qdrant collection for every consolidation operation. Add real-boundary startup, worker and collection isolation regressions.

commits.headline: fix(policy): align host tags and memory importance guidance
fix(recovery): preserve graph data during memory salvage
fix(openclaw): preserve omitted and explicit update tags
fix(mcp-sse): preserve connected legacy SSE sessions
fix(partners): mark the old board file copied even when nothing in it was kept
commits.body:
Local dev copies the old data/live/partners-pipeline.json into the store
on the first Partners request that finds nothing there. When the file
held only untouched seed deals, nothing was written, so the next request
ran the copy again. If a later checkout had changed one of those seed
deals by then, the file's old copy no longer matched the seed and was

editor had typed a review without saving and someone else saved that

older server through completed_at) could still get an AffiliateWP
payout and changed entries after it was finalized, which every other
entry write already refuses.

POST /api/v1/affiliates/payout-run/mark-paid (payouts:operate) runs the
shared mark-paid rules: parse, run, then checkMarkPaid on dry runs too, so
a paid, unapproved or stale entry never reaches the bridge. A confirm
sends markPaidKey as its idempotency key, and bridgeAnswer and
bridgeUnavailable map every answer the way the local route does.

commits.headline: fix(affiliates): bridgeAnswer reads the mu-plugin's WP_Error code too
commits.body:
The mu-plugin answers its own failures (bridge_exception, bad_signature,
bad_request, bridge_not_configured) as WP_Errors, which WordPress REST sends
as { code, message, data }, not { error }. bridgeAnswer read only `error`,
so the Worker would have reported a hosted bridge_exception as "no payout
id" and lost its "check AffiliateWP before any retry" message. It now takes
the code from `error` or `code`; a positive payout_id still wins.

commits.headline: feat(bridge): signed mark-paid plugin for wpfusion.com
commits.body:
A must-use plugin with one REST route, POST
/wp-json/wpf-dashboard/v1/affiliates/mark-paid, authenticated by an Ed25519
signature over METHOD\nPATH\nTIMESTAMP\nSHA256_HEX(body) with +-300 s skew.
WordPress holds only the public key (WPF_DASHBOARD_BRIDGE_PUBKEY); without it
every request is refused.

commits.headline: feat(worker): publish tokens limited to their domains
commits.body:
The publish route reads principal.publishDomains right after the body parses.
A non-null list that does not hold the requested domain answers 403
domain_not_allowed, naming the allowed domains (or saying none are allowed for

commits.headline: docs: clarify OpenClaw defaultTags update behavior and re-run notes
commits.body:
On an update the plugin sends the merged defaultTags list as the call's
tags and AutoMem replaces the memory's tags with it, so a tagless update
resets tags to defaultTags when defaultTags is non-empty. Also note that
env key copies (including blank values from a keyless install) are synced
to apiKey on a re-run, and that a default tag from an earlier install is
left as is when the slug is empty or ambiguous.

commits.headline: docs: correct why both secret stores are set
commits.body:
The stated reason — that the actor differs between opened/synchronize and
reopened, so those paths read different stores — rested on a wrong premise.
Dependabot's secret restriction covers pull_request, pull_request_review,
pull_request_review_comment, push, create, deployment and deployment_status; it
reaches pull_request_target only when the base ref of the PR was created by
Dependabot, which a bump opened against main is not. So pull_request_target runs
read Actions secrets normally.

commits.headline: docs: align Claude.ai web page with the AutoMem 0.16.2 MCP bridge (#401)
commits.body:
Streamable HTTP on the bridge is stateless: each /mcp request builds its own
server and transport with no session generator and no event store, so only
SSE keeps sessions and Last-Event-ID has no effect. Drop the resumability and
replay claims, the 1-hour TTL, and the full-duplex wording. State that the
memory service defaults PORT to 8001 instead of Flask's 5000, and keep the six
getAuthToken tiers separate from the route-level AUTOMEM_API_TOKEN fallback.

commits.headline: fix(deps): split vitest majors out of dev-toolchain-majors (#253)
commits.body:
A Dependabot group lands as one PR, so a single upstream peer ceiling
blocks every package in it. PR #214 bumped typescript 6.0.3 -> 7.0.2
together with vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 4 -> 5. typescript-eslint
caps at `peer typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0` in both its latest (8.72.0) and
canary (8.71.3-alpha.17) releases, so `npm ci` failed ERESOLVE and all
three CI jobs died at install before running anything. The vitest half
of that PR was fine on its own.

commits.headline: fix: disarm auto-merge before reclassifying, not after
commits.body:
GitHub keeps auto-merge armed when the pusher has write access — its docs say it
is disabled automatically only for pushes by users without write permission. So
from the moment a human commit, or a rebase into a major, landed until this job
reached its cancel step, the previous head's arm stayed live; if the new head's
required checks went green inside that window, GitHub could merge it before this
run had classified anything. The ordering was inherited from mcp-automem's
workflow, where the can

commits.headline: fix(ui): reapply behind an in-flight save, and never show error beside a conflict
commits.body:
A conflict's reapply() built its value on the winner's entry but, with another
save for the key in flight, sent it at that save's resulting version, so the
in-flight change was silently overwritten. The value and the version now share a
base: with a save in flight the reapply is built on what is on screen and queues
behind it.

commits.headline: docs: record that retry label trust is bound to the head
commits.body:

labels only once they are known to describe the current head, so a head that
changed from a patch bump to a major cannot be merged off the previous head's
automerge label.

commits.headline: fix: bind the retry pass's label trust to the head it is merging
commits.body:
The `workflow_run` pass cannot call `fetch-metadata`, so it reads the
classification the `pull_request_target` pass recorded as labels. Labels are
mutable and not bound to a commit, so a head that changed from a patch bump to a
major could be merged off the previous head's `automerge` label whenever CI
finished before classification had relabelled. The event-scoped concurrency
groups stop the two runs cancelling each other, but they do not order the label
write before the read.

commits.headline: fix(finance): the handover and take-back publish carries the status documents again
commits.body:
Leaving plaid-status and wise-status out of the state-only publish would delete the
host's status pointers when hosted finance is off, because a publish replaces its
whole domain. They are back in the bundle as on main; a malformed connection file
fails the publish loudly again. The data/live scan skip and the categorization guard
stay.

commits.headline: fix(finance): keep healthy status documents in the state publish, never print parser text
commits.body:
Leaving the Plaid and Wise status documents out of the handover and take-back
publish would delete the host's status panels when hosted finance is off, because a
publish replaces its whole domain. They are now built best effort instead:
a broken connection file costs only its own document, is reported by name without
the parser's message (which quotes the text around the break, and these files hold
credentials), and healthy ones go along. A bundle with no categorization document
in it is refused

commits.headline: fix(finance): the handover and take-back publish skips the connection-status inputs
commits.body:
The state-only publish still read and built the Plaid and Wise status documents
before the build was filtered to accounting-state, so a malformed plaid-items.json
or wise-config.json could fail a handover or take-back that sends only the three
categorization documents. includeStatus:false leaves them out; with hosted finance
on, which handover requires, the host drops those two documents from this publish
anyway.

commits.headline: fix(ui): run a Refresh's skipped ledger refetch when the last write settles
commits.body:
Refresh skipped the ledger-joined queries while a write was in flight,
leaving them to the catch-up. A write that starts no rebuild (a
dismissed rule suggestion) never runs one, so the freshly synced ledger
stayed cached. Refresh now records the skip, and whichever write settles
last runs it; the catch-up clears it when it refetches anyway.

commits.headline: fix(accounting): keep a failed catch-up rebuild retryable
commits.body:
The catch-up rebuild after an accept that finds the ledger behind keyed off
this request's already_reviewed skips. The guard has just marked those
cards stale, so if the rebuild failed nothing said so, and a retry found no
skip and never rebuilt. The check now reads the documents for the requested
rows that were neither accepted nor skipped for another reason, and a
failed catch-up answers 500, so retrying the same accept rebuilds.

commits.headline: fix(finance): a forced take-back reads the host only after it holds the lock
commits.body:
The host state was fetched before a forced take-back waited for the finance lock,
so a wait behind another finance command could leave it acting on an old view.
Everything is now read after the lock is held (marker first, then the host), so
it writes what the host says at that moment, and a host that moved to mode on
meanwhile is refused with nothing written. Dry runs and --staging still take no
lock.

commits.headline: fix(ui): let the catch-up finish a resumed wait, so a reload never keeps a stale ledger
commits.body:
A reload could read the ledger just before the rebuild landed, then see
the status already caught up and only forget the stored wait, leaving
the old ledger on screen. Resume the stored wait unconditionally and let
LedgerUpdating's poll and catch-up refetch the ledger and forget it.
This also drops the extra status request on mount.

commits.headline: fix(accounting): keep rules out of the guard for a manual entry's own category
commits.body:
A manual entry that carries a category is finalized before the walk, so no
rule ever reaches it. With unspecified German tax that row stays in the
inbox, and a matching rule made the guard call it reviewed: its cards went
stale and propose never targeted it again. The guard now skips the rule
check for such a row, and a test builds a ledger and checks that the guard
reviews none of the rows the rebuild left in needs_review.

commits.headline: fix(ui): resume only a rebuild this browser's own write is waiting on
commits.body:
state_rev > ledger_rev does not mean a rebuild is coming: proposals and
dismissals raise state_rev without one, so the reload bootstrap would
have shown "Ledger updating…" until the next 6-hour run. Keep the
pending revision in localStorage when a write flags a rebuild, resume
from it only while the served ledger is behind it, and forget it once
the ledger catches up. LedgerUpdating asks for the status only when a
wait is stored.

commits.headline: fix(finance): a forced take-back re-reads the marker once it holds the lock
commits.body:
finance:handover writes its marker under the finance lock and releases it before
its final publish. A forced take-back that started with no marker and queued
behind it then held the lock with a stale "no marker" and could overwrite the
local documents with the pre-handover host copy, republish, and remove the new
marker. Once the lock is held it now looks again and stops without changing
anything if a marker appeared.

commits.headline: fix(recall): measure a near-budget result before dropping it
commits.body:
The per-result estimate starts from the empty response, which still
carries the truncation notes that go away once every result fits. So a
result right at the budget was rejected, and a json result that fit
whole fell back to the compact shape or was dropped. When the estimate
says no, render and measure the real candidate before giving up.

commits.headline: fix(ui): say why the ledger failed to load instead of showing finance empty
commits.body:
After a handover with a missing or rejected viewer token, Transactions
read "No transactions in range": apiRequest dropped the response body
on a non-OK status, and no finance page looked at its query error. Reads
now fail through writeFailure, so the error carries the server's
sentence and code (remote_auth), with the old "API request failed"
text as the fallback. The finance pages show it and drop their empty
states while it stands.

commits.headline: fix(accounting): rebuild when an accept finds the ledger behind
commits.body:
If a local accept wrote the overrides but stopped before the proposals and
the rebuild, a retry skipped the card as already reviewed and rebuilt
nothing, so the row stayed in the inbox until some later write. The same
holds for a rule saved without a rebuild. Accept now rebuilds when it skips
a card as reviewed while the ledger still lists the row for review.

commits.body:

in the ~15 s rebuild window after a rule is saved, accepting AI cards for
rows the rule covers wrote overrides that then beat the rule for good,
where local dev skipped them as already reviewed.

commits.headline: fix(ui): refresh /me when a Plaid or Wise sync says the host owns finance
commits.body:
A local dashboard left open across finance:handover kept its Sync
buttons and lacked the upload-credentials note until a reload, because
useRuntime caches /me for the session and the 409 finance_host_owned did
not refresh it. The sync triggers now throw through writeFailure, so the
error carries its code and the server's sentence, and both connect
panels refresh /me on an ownership refusal. Refetching /me on window
focus was the alternative, but React Query v5 only listens for
visibilitychange,

commits.headline: fix(ui): give hosted reconciliation an optimistic step and error reporting
commits.body:
On the host a matched payout stayed in the unmatched queue until the
rebuild, so a second pick wrote a second reconciliation, and a failed
unmatch said nothing. A pick now takes the payout off the queue and adds
the manual match at once; unmatch marks the match until the rebuild drops
it; revertOptimistic puts reconciliations back on failure; and both
writes report errors on the page.

commits.headline: fix(ui): mount the ledger watcher before Vendors' and Reconciliation's early returns
commits.body:
Both pages returned their loading and empty states before FinanceSyncBar
mounted, so after a first manual expense Vendors could stay on "No
vendors yet" once the rebuild finished: nothing ran the catch-up that
refetches the ledger. A failed vendor write now says why instead of
reverting silently, and the stale vendor_meta comment describes today's
read and write path.

commits.headline: fix(accounting): refuse a patch with no field it may change
commits.body:
PATCH /accounting/transactions/:id with no allowed field saved an empty
override and started a rebuild; the account patch did the same with no
is_personal or display_name. Both now answer 400 bad_request before any
document is read. Every UI caller sends at least one field (TransactionsPage
sends category_id or scope, CashAccountsPage sends isPersonal or a string
displayName), so nothing relied on the empty patch.

test matches its constraint error, and a new test covers the updated_by
foreign key in both directions.

commits.headline: fix(ui): keep the owner's Refresh off the served ledger mid-rebuild
commits.body:
Refresh invalidated every query, so a ledger still behind the owner's
last write was refetched and its optimistic rows reverted until the
catch-up. While a rebuild is awaited or a write is in flight, Refresh
now leaves the ledger-joined queries to the catch-up.

commits.headline: docs(worker): reword the accounting publish refusal for the operator
commits.body:
It told the Mac to publish accounting-state only, which is no longer the
whole story now that the host can own categorization too. It now says the
host syncs accounting and that categorization is a separate publish while
the Mac still owns it.

commits.headline: docs(finance): take-back order, staging side effects, and which edits rebuild the ledger
commits.body:
Update the runbook and spec for the new take-back order (marker kept through the
republish, lock when forced, a bare npm --force only matters with no marker), say
plainly that a staging handover writes the real marker and removes the real
launchd agent, list exactly which hosted edits start a ledger rebuild (taken from
the worker's route flags), and put the handover's marker check before its test GET
as the code does.

commits.headline: fix(worker): validate the rule preview first, and report rebuilt on every rebuilding write
commits.body:
The rule preview read the ledger and three source-bag snapshots, then
validated its body. It now refuses a bad body with testRule's own message
before reading anything, and reads only the ledger snapshot. The rest of
the Task 2 ordering item stays: the pure write functions check ctx.ledger
as a value, so reading it later needs a shared change.

commits.headline: fix(accounting): a repeat rule-suggestion dismiss writes nothing
commits.body:
Dismissing a key that is already dismissed returned the overrides anyway.
Locally that rewrote the file; on the host it added a state revision and a
document version with no audit row, which also made take-back's no-change
shortcut miss. A repeat now returns no documents.

commits.headline: fix(ui): resume "Ledger updating…" after a reload mid-rebuild
commits.body:
The pending revision lived only in memory, so a tab reloaded or opened
while the host was still building the owner's last write showed the old
ledger and never polled. On mount, the owner's LedgerUpdating asks
/accounting/ledger/status once and waits on state_rev when it is ahead
of ledger_rev.

commits.headline: fix(finance): publish:snapshots reports the categorization it left out
commits.body:
When the host owned categorization and nothing else was left to send,
publish:snapshots exited before --report-json, so refresh:finance read no file
and called the run "published (no report)". Domains left out locally were also
missing from the results. The core now returns them as skipped entries in
publishAll's shape and the CLI writes the report for that run too. Quiet mode
still prints only failures and the summary, as documented.

commits.headline: fix(accounting): read each file only when a write needs it
commits.body:
applyLocal parsed overrides, manual entries and AI proposals before every
mutation, so a corrupt proposals file made an unrelated transaction edit
answer 500. The documents, and the ledger for the routes that check it,
now load on first use, after the request's own checks. The rule preview
takes a ledger loader for the same reason, and the account patch checks
its body before it reads the overrides.

commits.headline: fix(ui): skip the ledger catch-up while any accounting write is in flight
commits.body:
useIsMutating's count is from LedgerUpdating's last render, so a write
started between that render and the effect slipped past the deferral and
the catch-up refetched the served ledger under its optimistic row.
catchUpLedger now checks the live count too.

commits.headline: fix(finance): refresh:finance re-checks the handover once it holds the lock
commits.body:
The stand-down was checked only before the lock wait. finance:handover writes
its marker under that lock, so a refresh queued behind it went on to sync Plaid
and Wise locally after the marker existed (publish re-checked, the pulls did
not). lockUnlessHandedOver checks before the wait and again once the lock is
held, and gives the lock back when it stands down. The CLI contract test now also
pins that the answer is acted on, not just where the guard sits.

commits.headline: fix(ui): refetch the ledger once the last accounting write settles with nothing to wait for
commits.body:
Two writes stacked on one row that both failed could leave the first
write's unsaved category on screen, in either failure order: the later
write's before snapshot already holds the earlier patch, and the cache
stores a structurally shared copy of what it reverts to, so identity
checks miss. A hosted write that flags no rebuild likewise left its row
marked updating. When no rebuild is pending and no other write is in
flight, the served ledger is the truth, so refetch it.

commits.headline: fix(worker): break ledger status ties by start time, and pin its other cases
commits.body:
Two runs that finish in the same millisecond made last_error depend on
scan order. It now takes the one that started later, then the later row.
Also pins the generic message for a failed run with no recorded error, a
running rebuild not hiding the failure before it, and the mode-on ledger,
proposals and status routes reading the D1 documents.

commits.headline: fix(recall): refuse a token budget too small for an empty response
commits.body:
With every droppable diagnostic gone, the response that is left (counts,
mode, paging, the header) is the smallest one possible. A budget below
it, such as AUTOMEM_RECALL_TOKEN_BUDGET=1, used to fall through and
return that response over the bound. Throw a clear "raise it" error
instead. ID fetches stay exempt.

commits.headline: test(dev): drive the finance gate through the real middleware
commits.body:
createMockApiMiddleware now takes the marker reader and the local route
handlers, so tests can run the actual gate with spies instead of real Plaid,
Wise or accounting handlers. Covers gate position against hosted mode and the
local handlers, proxy and 502 with no token, refused writes (matched or not) and
bank syncs, the marker being read on every request, and local /me before and
after handover. The Plaid exchange skip is pinned as text because its handler
writes data/secure.

commits.headline: fix(worker): reseed instead of dereferencing a document the flip deleted
commits.body:
loadAccountingState seeded missing documents and read again, assuming the
second read found them. A flip DELETE landing in between left a document
missing and the read failed with a TypeError (a 500). It now loops: a
repeat reseeds, a take-back in between answers from the snapshots, and
documents that keep vanishing end in a clear error. The reseed test also
asserts rowid and version, not just updated_at.

useMutation wrapper. Pin today's lifecycle: the optimistic patch, the
pending revision, rollback, the error callback and the /me refresh.

commits.headline: fix(finance): take-back keeps the marker through the republish and locks when forced
commits.body:
Take-back removed the marker before the production republish, so with the dev
server up a local edit in those seconds could be missing from the bundle. The
marker now stays until the republish has ended and goes on success or on a
handled failure, so the recovery command still works. A forced take-back with no
marker takes the finance lock for the same window. A bare npm --force no longer
stops every take-back: with a marker --force does nothing, so the npm_config_force
refusal moved into the no

commits.headline: fix(worker): refuse unknown documents and pin the versions a write read
commits.body:
A document name outside DOC_NAMES, or a row deleted between the read and
the commit, made the document UPDATE match nothing while the gate and the
audit row still committed: a write answered success and saved nothing. The
helper now throws on an unknown name, and the gate holds only while every
document being written is still the version it read, so a vanished row
retries against the reseeded documents.

commits.headline: feat(finance): let a state-only publish skip the data/live scan
commits.body:

wanted only the accounting-state domain, so an unrelated file that failed the
secret scan failed the whole build. includeLive:false skips that scan and still
reads the two Wise files wise-status needs.

invented rebuild failures no longer print stack traces.

commits.headline: fix(worker): a ledger start that throws after its take keeps the rebuild queued
commits.body:
startRun cleared ledger_pending in its take batch, then read the run row
and created the workflow. A throw from the read, or from the cleanup after
a failed create, left the flag at 0 and the edit unqueued until the next
full run. Everything after the take is now inside the try, and the flag is
put back even when the cleanup fails.

commits.headline: fix(finance): parse the marker host as an https origin, warn once, say when it cannot be read
commits.body:
The marker host was checked with startsWith('https://') and then stripped, so
"https://" passed as "https:" and local reads went to https:/api/v1/...
(host "api") carrying the viewer token. Parse it with URL, require https and a
name, refuse credentials, and keep only the origin. A bad marker also warned on
every request and blamed a missing host for any read error; it now warns once
per distinct problem and names the read error.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): humanize activity tree durations past a minute
commits.body:
Running steps in the chat activity tree aged with the latency formatter,
which counts raw seconds without bound, so a tool step running for half an
hour read 1859s. Match the Tools row fix: keep latency precision under a
minute (684ms, 42.3s) and switch to the compact age stamp past it (1m, 30m,
2h, 3d).

commits.headline: fix(replay): stop restoring the --hold view after operator input
commits.body:
--tab and --palette set the initial view. Under --hold the wrapper kept
restoring them on every later conversation reset, so an operator who had
closed the palette or changed tab would be pulled back to the flags.

commits.headline: refactor(workspace): drop write-only legacy workspace state
commits.body:
The last pass removed what deadcode and U1000 can see. This one removes
state that the tick, sync and key paths still write but that no live V2
surface reads.

commits.headline: Fixture fix, workflow hygiene
fix(replay): detect conversation resets with a model counter
commits.body:
e866ce9 inferred a reset from the conversation id changing away from a
non-empty value. That misses a fixture whose first conversation event
is a successful conversation.new ack: the id moves from empty, but
applyConversationNewAck still clears the workspace back to chat.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): humanize Tools durations past a minute
commits.body:
The Tools row duration cell used the latency formatter, which counts raw
seconds without bound, so a background agent running for two hours read
7200s. Keep the latency precision under a minute (684ms, 2.3s) and switch
to the compact age stamp past it (1m, 30m, 2h, 51d), the same one the
agent cards use.

commits.headline: fix(fixtures): date workspace-v2 agent events on the Hub snapshot clock
commits.body:
Replay's clock is the newest envelope, the 2026-09-23T08:00:01Z Hub
snapshot. The agent events spliced in from agents-session.jsonl were still
dated 2026-08-02, so their running rows in the Tools tab aged 4469977s
(about 52 days). Shift their ts and startedAt by one constant offset to
2026-09-23 07:50-07:55, keeping content and spacing. File order stays
monotonic: the memory lines at 00:00, then the agents, then the snapshot.

commits.headline: revert(workspace): keep the composer's attention version after a conflict
commits.body:
Reverts 3134a129f3. Adopting the refreshed task's attention version on a
failed send let an edited retry answer a question the operator had not
seen: below 120 columns a reply can be composed from the agent list
with the detail pane hidden, so nothing shows the new question.

commits.headline: feat(workspace): say SLEEPING on the v2 dock while the runtime sleeps
commits.body:
The live Workspace v2 frame only said "sleeping" during the 1.5 s s-key
flash from #122. After it, a sleeping runtime read "● IDLE" in yellow:
inactive health always replaces the phase, so even AutoHub's own
phase:"SLEEPING" never reached the dock.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): retry a conflicted reply against the refreshed question
commits.body:
When a reply fails because the pending question changed, Client.Act
returns the refreshed task and its error says to review the question
before sending the draft. The model stored that task, so the detail pane
showed the new question, but the composer kept the attention version
captured when it opened. Editing and pressing Enter therefore hit the
same conflict every time.

commits.headline: fix(replay): keep --tab and --palette across a conversation switch
commits.body:
replay applied --tab and --palette before the fixture played. A
conversation.snapshot with a new id, or a conversation.new ack, runs
clearConversationWorkspaceState, which puts the workspace back on chat
and drops palette mode to NORMAL. So every --tab replay of
workspace-v2-session and operator-trace-session rendered chat, and so
did the make visual captures built on them (logs, runtime, tools,
inspector, agents).

commits.headline: fix(workspace): name the bridge's offline cause in the V2 dock
commits.body:
With the bridge disconnected or exited, the V2 dock read only
"● OFFLINE". The cause lived in the legacy header, which V2 does not
draw. The dock state label now appends it as a muted segment:
"● OFFLINE · bridge disconnected".

commits.headline: fix(workspace): handle G, space and l in the V2 Memory tab
commits.body:
These three keys fell through workspaceV2MemoryKey to the legacy
workspaceMemoryKey. It moved MemoryCursor and its expansion map, which
nothing draws, so the keys did nothing visible.

to send guidance and type a draft. At 80 columns the draft overflows and

Each blink phase lasts 250 ms, so the 125 ms gap could land both shots in

8 fps frame grid, so the script requires the 150x38 pair to differ
(capturing again, three attempts in all) and the reduced-motion pair to
match.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): key the agent prompt off its own action notice
commits.body:
Hub.Notice is shared with unrelated UI: a workspace preferences save
failure writes it too. While an agent compose was open, such a notice
replaced the draft, made Enter refuse a valid send, and was wiped by the
next keystroke.

an intra-function dead branch, so everything it called still looked live: the
tab-strip hit-test (workspaceTabAtX, workspaceTabStripZones) against a strip
that is no longer drawn, the input-dock click, the sidecar clicks and the

including workspaceClickTranscript. V2 resolves tr

commits.headline: fix(workspace): hold Enter while a hub notice hides the agent draft
commits.body:
After a failed reply or redirect the dock shows the failure notice in
place of the draft and advertises "type to edit · esc cancel", but Enter
still resent the hidden draft with the attention version captured when
the compose began. After a "question changed" conflict that repeats a
request already known to be stale. Enter now waits until an edit clears
the notice, so it only ever sends the draft the operator can see.

commits.headline: feat(workspace): draw the s sleep/listen flash on the v2 frame
commits.body:
The flash from #112 and #114 lived only in the legacy chip row and
statusline, which the live Workspace v2 frame never drew. The state was
live (the next s toggles from it, and the tick raises the frame rate for
it), but nothing showed it.

commits.headline: fix(release): publish a public manifest from the private repo root
commits.body: npm refuses a private workspace package. The release job now writes dist/package.json without private or workspaces, and the repo root stays private.

commits.headline: fix(cockpit): ignore acks from a superseded default pin too
commits.body:
A late model.set_default ack for a pin a newer ctrl+d replaced would
overwrite StatusHint and announce the older model as the default while
the catalog and the star show the newer one. The superseded-pin guard
now covers acknowledgements as well as errors.

commits.headline: Prettier
fix(workspace): show hub action errors in the agent dock while composing
commits.body:
The Agents-tab dock row showed Hub.Notice only when no compose was active.
Once a reply, redirect or stop failed and kept its draft, the row went back
to "To X › draft▌" and the reason ("question changed · not retried") was
drawn nowhere. The removed legacy footer was the only place that showed it.
The recovery confirmation had the same gap for "· retry confirmation
retained".

commits.headline: fix(cockpit): ignore errors from a superseded default pin
commits.body:
A model.set_default command.error for a ctrl+d that a newer pin replaced
no longer reaches StatusHint, LastError or the optimistic star. The
newest dispatched pin id is kept apart from PendingModelDefault because
any model.catalog clears the pending pin, and a genuine error for the
latest pin can arrive after one.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): move the Tools highlight on list jump keys
commits.body:

workspaceV2ToolsKey to the legacy list handler, which moved only
WorkspaceState.ToolsCursor. V2 renders and opens V2.ToolSelectedID, so
the highlight stayed put while Enter synced from the hidden cursor and
opened a different row (G then Enter: tool-49 lit, tool-00 opened).

fix(cli): keep formatted secrets out of step snapshots
commits.body: Evaluate steps with padded op names skipped the source guard, so secrets were substituted into code. Trim the op first. Snapshot values that only insert separators into a secret are redacted too.

commits.headline: fix(cli): skip covered controls in snapshot refs and role clicks
commits.body: Role and ref clicks now use the same visibility check as text clicks, including one parent frame when the control sits in a nested iframe. Snapshot refs use that check too, so a hidden frame or an overlay is not a click target.

commits.headline: fix(cli): keep snapshot roots and names inside the right tree
commits.body: An empty href is still a link, a hidden main is not the snapshot root, and a custom-element main or dialog walks its own shadow root. Label lookup can see a sibling outside main, but it stops at the shadow root.

commits.headline: fix(brand): crop the toolbar glove to the solid bone
commits.body: The bright cyan plume passed the luminance row test, so the crop still included the wrist trail. Count low-chroma bone only, and clear the trail that hangs beside the longer fingers.

commits.headline: fix(cli): bound steps and keep snapshot and evaluate data
commits.body: Evaluate source is no longer rewritten by placeholder substitution, snapshot url and title stay in the step result, and the command deadline stops the sequence.

commits.headline: fix(cli): keep validation alerts in the scoped snapshot
commits.body: The scoped payload dropped role=alert and .error text, so a post-write snapshot could hide a failure like Card declined.

commits.headline: fix(cli): keep nav shadows out and name range inputs
commits.body: Slider and spinbutton inputs were published as textboxes, and a control inside a nav web component leaked into the default snapshot.

commits.headline: fix(brand): clear only the plume under the wrist
commits.body: A color wipe was eating the cyan rim on the glove and leaving the gray smoke on the inactive mark. Only pixels below the last solid row are the plume.

commits.headline: fix(cli): group an existing tab when goto sets a title
commits.body: goto --group-title without --page-name used the current http tab and dropped the title. It now asks the extension to group that tab.

commits.headline: fix(brand): clear mist pixels inside the glove crop
commits.body: Cyan mist overlapping the glove rectangle was enlarged with the glove and left a wrist trail on the toolbar icon.

commits.headline: fix(cli): substitute step placeholders and keep evaluate fields
commits.body: Fill and type steps were sending {me:} and {secure:} literals, and an evaluate result named url or title was stripped with the operation wrapper.

commits.headline: fix(cli): refuse covered role clicks and publish implicit roles
commits.body: Role and ref clicks now use the same visibility hit-test as text clicks, and range, number, and multi-select controls keep their slider, spinbutton, and listbox roles.

commits.headline: fix(cli): keep snapshot names, refs, and expanded state
commits.body: aria-labelledby was empty on element snapshot roots, full-snapshot nav refs restarted at e1, and a click that only toggled aria-expanded reported no state change.

commits.headline: fix(extension): fall back when a cached tab group cannot be reused
fix(cli): resolve role clicks with the default snapshot refs
commits.body: Role and name clicks were numbered across the whole page, so an ambiguity candidate ref could activate a different control than snapshot --ref. Both paths now use the dialog-plus-main scope.

commits.headline: fix(cli): omit password values from snapshot nodes
commits.body: A password input's current value is a credential, so the scoped snapshot publishes the control without that value.

commits.headline: feat(cli): pass an optional tab group title
commits.body: open and goto forward --group-title to the relay. A blank title is ignored, so existing opens stay on the Browser Hand group.

commits.headline: feat(cli): run a form as one steps call
commits.body: A repeated click, fill, and evaluate sequence stops at the first miss, and --quiet keeps the step results without the page wrapper.

commits.headline: feat(cli): wire scoped snapshot, compact doctor, and click handles
commits.body: Snapshot defaults to the open dialog plus main, doctor stays status-sized unless --verbose, and click accepts --ref or --role and --name and reports whether the control state changed.

commits.headline: feat(cli): add snapshot, doctor, and click contract helpers
commits.body: Page snapshot and click resolution live in a module whose selectors are inlined when the expression is injected. Doctor shaping returns the active tab unless verbose.

commits.headline: docs(skill): describe the 0.7.2 agent contract
commits.body: Document compact doctor, scoped snapshots, click handles, steps, quiet output, tab groups, and the dismissed debugger infobar.

commits.headline: feat(extension): add an optional titled tab group
commits.body: A groupTitle on open starts a Chrome tab group in a random palette color other than grey. The relay forwards that title through Target.createTarget.

commits.headline: fix(extension): leave a dismissed debugger bar dismissed
commits.body: Cancel on the infobar is canceled_by_user. Keep the tab in the session and serve later commands over the scripting transport instead of reattaching.

commits.body: The status dot is drawn on the glove so the 16px active and inactive icons stay readable.

They now fall through to the PFC mapping, as on the Mac today.

a failing bank also shows on its item row and the Cash banner, so if the
limit has to cut something, it cuts bank notes.

commits.headline: fix(finance): the dotenv guard also catches dotenv's KEY: value form
commits.body:
wrangler parses .env and .env.local with the dotenv package, which accepts
`KEY: value` as well as `KEY=value`. util.parseEnv only reads the latter, so
`CLOUDFLARE_ENV: staging` would have passed the I1 guard while wrangler still
applied it. A line-anchored check for the key with dotenv's two separators

commits.headline: fix(finance): do not refresh Plaid freshness when no bank refreshed
commits.body:
A Wise-only success republished the unchanged bank rows with a new
synced_at. Freshness is the oldest anchor, so the dashboard read "Synced 5m
ago" over stale bank data. The two Plaid snapshots are now written only when
a bank merged or an upload unlinked a bank whose rows were dropped; the
ledger is still rebuilt from the served rows.

commits.headline: fix(finance): advance a Plaid cursor only from the delta the ledger merged
commits.body:
The step returned next_cursor and accounts while the ledger merged whatever
the R2 object held, so a step attempt that timed out and wrote late could
leave the ledger with one attempt's rows and the item with another's cursor.
Each attempt now writes its delta (with the cursor and the stripped accounts
inside it) under its own key, buildRunLedger reports the deltas it merged,
and publish advances cursors from that list only.

commits.headline: fix(finance): upload-credentials refuses a dotenv CLOUDFLARE_ENV and never echoes a parse error
commits.body:
wrangler loads .env and .env.local from its cwd and takes its target from
CLOUDFLARE_ENV there, which bypassed the shell-only guard: production secrets
could reach the staging Worker. The CLI now refuses (exit 2, naming the file,
never a value) when either file defines the key, even empty.

commits.headline: feat(finance): refresh:finance waits up to 15 minutes for the lock
commits.body:
A busy lock made refresh:finance exit 75 at once, so a scheduled run that
landed during a local AI propose run, which can hold the lock for
minutes, was pushed out by a whole 6-hour interval.

commits.headline: fix(finance): take the finance lock for accounting edits
commits.body:
The /accounting/* write routes (transaction and account edits, manual
entries, rules, vendor meta, reconciliation, AI propose, accept and
dismiss) rewrite overrides, manual entries and AI proposals and rebuild
the ledger without the finance lock. An edit during a scheduled refresh
could interleave two rebuilds, or publish new state beside a ledger
built from the old one.

commits.headline: fix(finance): reclaim a stale lock without deleting a live one
commits.body:
Reclaiming read the holder, compared it, then unlinked the path. Between
the read and the unlink another process could reclaim the same stale lock
and create its own, and the unlink then removed that live lock, leaving
two writers. Release had the same read-then-unlink shape.

commits.headline: fix(finance): lock every Plaid item mutation; spot worktrees; quiet publish
commits.body:
Link, rename and disconnect in local dev rewrite plaid-items.json too, so a
scheduled refresh that read the store first could write it back stale and
restore a disconnected bank. They now take the finance lock (link before the
Plaid exchange, so a busy lock never drops a new token) and answer 409 while a
refresh holds it.

commits.headline: docs: design hosted finance sync (Phase 5a)
commits.body:
Phase 5 splits into 5a (finance syncing on the host) and 5b (finance writes).
5a moves Plaid and Wise sync and the ledger rebuild to a Cloudflare Workflow on
a 6h cron plus an owner-only Refresh, with credentials encrypted on the Mac and
written via wrangler, and a shadow mode so the first hosted ledger is compared
with a local rebuild before it serves anything.

commits.headline: feat(finance): add npm run refresh:finance
commits.body:
Syncs Plaid and Wise under the finance lock, rebuilds the ledger once, then
publishes the accounting domains through publish-snapshots. The step rules
(skip unconfigured sources, publish only when something refreshed, never
publish after a failed rebuild) live in refresh-finance-core with injected
steps so they are unit-tested. A busy lock exits 75 so launchd retries.

commits.headline: feat(finance): add a finance lock and take it in the dev sync jobs

data/secure/.finance-sync.lock keeps the scheduled refresh and a Sync click
in local dev from rewriting accounting-* and the Plaid cursor at the same
time. A busy lock finishes the dev job at once with exit_code 1 and the
holder in its output.

commits.headline: fix(worker): read accounting views from one generation and count UTF-8 bytes
commits.body:
- The transaction detail and AI proposal views resolve the ledger, Plaid
  transactions and Wise pointers in one D1 query (readSnapshots). An
  accounting publish that commits mid-request can no longer pair a ledger
  from one run with source data from the next.
- Publish stores each envelope as UTF-8 bytes, so snapshot_pointers.bytes,
  the audit entry and the publish response report the stored size instead
  of a UTF-16 length.
- Tests: a publish injected between pointer reads, and a non-ASCII

commits.headline: docs: disclose published customer PII and set WPF_REMOTE_API in step 6
commits.body:
publish:snapshots uploads every top-level data/live file, including the
EDD files that carry customer names and emails. SYNC.md said those never
leave the machine. It and DEPLOY.md now say they go to the private,
Access-gated R2 bucket (principals only) and that staging gets fixtures.

commits.headline: fix(publish): keep accounting-state slugs out of the live-directory pass
commits.body:
A state file found in data/live (accounting-overrides, plaid-status, ...)
still published under accounting-state, so includeState:false (--no-state)
could return a state bundle and a stale live copy could publish when the
secure source was absent. The live pass now checks PUBLISHED_LIVE_SLUGS
only; state publishes solely from data/secure.

commits.headline: fix(worker): cap publish bodies at 10 MB and decode them as they stream
commits.body:
A 50 MB body could not fit a 128 MB Worker isolate once it was decoded,
parsed and re-serialised per envelope, and readTextWithin held every raw
chunk plus a combined copy before decoding.

commits.headline: docs(deploy): publish bodies are capped at 10 MB
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(publish): publish only an explicit allowlist of data/live slugs
commits.body:
A valid filename was treated as permission to publish, so operational
exports that share data/live (presale and renewal outreach queues, CRM
sync audits, the payout queue, customer-health-by-email) would upload
customer PII in the edd bundle. PUBLISHED_LIVE_SLUGS now lists the files
the hosted copy reads: the file-backed UI endpoints, the accounting view
inputs and the freshness anchors. A contract test fails when a UI
endpoint or freshness anchor is missing from it.

commits.headline: docs(deploy): say that unpublished domains keep their snapshot
commits.body:
A domain publish drops the endpoints its bundle omits, and only for that
domain: domains left out by --domain or --no-state, or with no local
files, are not sent and keep their last snapshot.

fix(worker): make principal identities unique regardless of case
commits.body:
Lookups already ignored case, but the UNIQUE constraint did not, so
Steve@example.com and steve@example.com could both be seeded and the token
would resolve to whichever row came first. The column is now COLLATE NOCASE,
which also makes the plain equality lookup case-insensitive.

commits.headline: fix(worker): cap publish bodies on the bytes read, not Content-Length
commits.body:
Content-Length is optional on streamed uploads and unchecked when malformed,
so the 50 MB cap could be bypassed before the body was buffered. Read the
body through readTextWithin, which stops at the limit. Tests cover both
fixes.

commits.headline: fix(worker): a domain publish drops pointers for slugs it no longer has
commits.body:
A publish carries the whole domain, so a slug missing from the bundle (its
local file was removed) now loses its pointer in the same D1 batch. The
hosted copy then reads it as not connected, as local dev does, instead of
serving the last snapshot indefinitely. Other domains are untouched.

commits.headline: fix(dev): require https for the hosted API the local proxy reads
commits.body:
The viewer service token travels on every proxied request, so refuse a
plain-http WPF_REMOTE_API unless it points at localhost. A test now pins the
proxy's redirect: 'manual' guard, so a redirect cannot carry the token to
another host.

commits.headline: fix(worker): log why Access rejects a token and keep routes under /api/

Log the jose error code (never the token or its claims) when an Access token
is rejected, so a misconfigured audience or team domain shows in the Worker
logs instead of a bare 401. The route registry now refuses a path outside
/api/: authentication and CSRF middleware are mounted there, so such a route
would skip both.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): surface palette sleep/wake errors after an s toggle
commits.body:
The stale-error filter compared against the key toggle's command id, so a
rejected palette sleep or wake (different id) was dropped as stale after any
earlier s press. Track the newest sleep/wake dispatch from every source:
an error is stale only when it names an older dispatch, and the flash is
cleared only by the key toggle's own error.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): cover the initial key-repeat delay and honor reduced motion
commits.body:
The first auto-repeat of a held s lands after the terminal's initial
repeat delay (~0.5s on macOS), outside the 250ms cadence window, so holding
s toggled sleep then wake. Hold the first key after an accepted press to a
750ms initial window, then slide the 250ms window once a repeat stream is
recognised.

commits.body:

response it actually assembles. No behavior change: the existing recall

commits.headline: docs(agents): drop ranked offset from the recall_memory contract
