steer an agent into the new rejection. Say that ranked recall has no
offset and to raise `limit` instead.

commits.headline: fix(client): accept a Unicode zero as the start of a 0x prefix
commits.body:
Python's int() reads every Unicode decimal digit as its ASCII value
before parsing, so uuid.UUID("٠x" + 30 hex digits) is valid: "٠x" is a
radix prefix. The regex only recognized an ASCII "0x" and refused that
spelling. Capture the prefix digit and accept it when it is a zero.
Unicode encodes each decimal digit set as a contiguous 0-9 run, so a
digit's value is its distance from the start of its run, mod 10.

commits.headline: fix(recall): mark outside-scope results and keep relation endpoints in compact output
commits.body:
Text output never said which results scope_fallback admitted from
outside the requested tags, and items output dropped the notes
entirely. Mark each such result with " [outside tag scope]" in text and
items and "Outside tag scope: true" in detailed, the hosted bridge's
old wording. items carries the notes in its trailing block, so its
per-memory blocks keep their one-to-one order with `results`.

commits.headline: fix(recall): keep t_valid, t_invalid and archived in json and ID-fetch output
commits.body:
Result normalization copied a fixed field list and dropped the node
state that explains why a current_only: false or state_mode: "history"
recall returned a memory. Map t_valid, t_invalid and archived on the
ranked, ID-fetch and enumeration paths, and emit them in the unbudgeted
outputs (format: "json" and ID fetch). Budgeted text/items/detailed
stay compact.

commits.headline: fix(client): refuse memory ids the API would reject before they reach a URL path
commits.body:
fetchMemoryById, updateMemory and deleteMemory put the caller's id
straight into the request path. encodeURIComponent stops "/", "?" and
"#" but not "." or a whole segment that names another route, so
"by-tag" reached GET and DELETE /memory/by-tag and ".." normalized to
"/". None of these returned or deleted data, but the next route added
under /memory/ would be reachable by id.

commits.headline: fix(recall): reject params a recall mode cannot honor and correct the schema
commits.body:
Enumeration mode (`exhaustive: true`) now rejects context, language,
active_path, context_tags, context_types, priority_ids and
per_query_limit. GET /memory/by-tag reads only tags, limit and offset,
so these were silently ignored and an audit looked prioritized when it
was not.

commits.headline: fix(recall): return recall errors as isError tool results
commits.body:
The recall_memory case returned buildRecallMemoryResponse's promise from
inside the handler's try without awaiting it, so a rejection skipped the
catch and reached clients as a JSON-RPC -32603 error. Await it so recall
failures come back as `Error: <msg>` with isError: true, like the other
five tools.

commits.body:
The comments and parity doc said ".." normalizes to a viewer at "/"
whose HTML would be read back as a memory. The viewer moved to /viewer,
and GET / is now a JSON 404, so ".." reads as an unknown id and "by-tag"
gets GET /memory/by-tag's 400. Neither returns data. The pre-check stays:
the id lands in the URL path, and any route added under /memory/ later
would be reachable the same way.

issue (#225 to #230), and add the two Codex found after the list was

response budget trims enumeration pages but keeps has_more (#230).

commits.headline: fix(mcp-sse): accept every memory_id the API's uuid.UUID accepts
commits.body:
The memory_id pre-check only took the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 form, so the
bridge refused ids the API accepts and stdio forwards: braces, a urn:uuid:
prefix, no hyphens, and the int(s, 16) grammar uuid.UUID parses with (0x,
underscores, whitespace, Unicode digits). It now applies that rule.

commits.body:

transports for reasons unrelated to either: enrichment summaries, JIT

other's, and the recency score moves with the clock. The live recall check
now compares outcomes instead (error message, mode, paging, and which
fixtures came back in what order). Rendering stays pinned byte for byte by
test/recall-parity.test.js. The redaction also covers the recency

commits.body:

writing to a clock after its first failed POST in a tick, and forgets that
clock's confirmed values so everything is rewritten once it answers. A
non-UTF-8 command file is now deleted instead of crash-looping the daemon,

write with a 60 s re-assert, writes notice.json once per verdict, and runs

directory, the health probe, status.json, and state.json; --once renders one
pass and exits. desk_core tolerates a persisted blocked entry without color.

edited flag: showing or hiding the rail before the load keeps the
operator's visibility but still takes the file's panes and width, so the
write-back can no longer erase saved panes. A dismissed drawer (Esc) is

commits.body:
IdlessOptionalEndpointEventsDeduplicateAcrossRefreshesWithoutServerCursors
asserted endpoint.Served.IsCompleted straight after the second fetch.
UnityWebRequest completes on the last Content-Length byte, which can land
before the fixture's thread-pool continuation disposes the client and
exits, so a busy full suite occasionally saw an unfinished task and
failed with a bare "Expected: True But was: False".

whole rail edited, which would have discarded the file's panes. Panes and
width now carry their own pre-load edited flags: the load takes only the
untouched parts from the file and writes back when anything was edited.

commits.headline: fix(voice): claim Chatterbox children at spawn time, not at settle
commits.body:
The bounded shutdown wait narrowed the leak but could not close it: a cold
start slower than the cap still exits with a live Python child, and neither a
latch nor a kill-on-timeout can help, because after process.exit() no code
runs and settle-time ownership has no handle to kill before then.

commits.headline: fix(voice): keep the shutdown wait timer ref'd
commits.body:
An unref'd deadline timer lets Node exit naturally while the shutdown wait is
still awaiting a pending warm, skipping the stop the wait exists to reach and
turning a failed shutdown's exit 1 into a natural 0. The timer is always
cleared and the only caller exits immediately after, so unref bought nothing.

commits.headline: fix(voice): wait for a pending lazy warm before Chatterbox teardown
commits.body:
A lazy Chatterbox warm spawns its Python child long before it settles, and
the handle only reaches start-voice-server's ownership variable from the
warmer's settle handlers. Shutdown stopped whatever it already held and then
called process.exit in the same tick, so a warm still pending at teardown
stranded a serving child holding the GPU and its port.

commits.body:
Codex P1 on #400: NSPredicate's MATCHES operator isn't supported against
the SQLite store, so the previous fix could make every
requiresUserAttentionPredicate() fetch throw instead of filter (Inbox,
Sidebar, watch snapshot). Revert the predicate to its SQLite-safe exact
"!= ''" form and close the whitespace-only gap at the actual entry point
instead: RemoteTask's attentionType decode now normalizes (trim,
blank-to-nil) via the same firstNonEmpty helper already used for
attentionMessage/resultSum

commits.headline: fix(tasks): reject whitespace-only attentionType in predicate too
commits.body:
Codex review on #400: hasUnresolvedAttention trims via nilIfEmpty, so a
whitespace-only attentionType (e.g. "  \n\t ") is treated as unset. The
predicate's exact "!= ''" check missed that case. Switch to a MATCHES
check against the whole-string whitespace pattern so both "" and any
all-whitespace value are rejected, matching the property. Extends the
regression test with a whitespace-only case.

commits.headline: fix(tasks): align requiresUserAttentionPredicate with requiresUserAttention
commits.body:
Task.requiresUserAttentionPredicate() disagreed with the requiresUserAttention
property on two edges: a nil status (the property treats it as .pending via
the taskStatus fallback, the predicate excluded it entirely) and an
empty-string attentionType (the property's hasUnresolvedAttention uses
nilIfEmpty and treats it as unset, the predicate counted it as set). Fixes #398.

commits.headline: fix(web): let the voice client follow the server's TTS provider (#1718)
commits.body:
The web voice client pinned Chatterbox. Its constructor set `provider =
'chatterbox'` and it sent `provider:set { provider: 'chatterbox' }` on
every connect, a leftover from when Chatterbox was the fixed primary.
Whenever Chatterbox is configured, the server honors that per-session
override, so browser voice ignored `VOICE_HYBRID_TTS_PROVIDER`. With
Qwen3-TTS becoming the default (#1717, owner decision 2026-09-21), the
browser lane would have stayed on Chatterbox.

All three production readers pass `skipCap: true` so a cold reseed can
recover a deliberately over-cap deferred batch after a restart (thread

the read honored it for any oversized blob — including a legacy session with
124 grants. Combined with the cold seed's unconditional `deferEviction`, such
a session cold-seeded uncapped, and since a keyword-free turn never performs
an ordinary merge it could keep sending that pool

prs.title: fix(enrichment): preserve concurrent memory updates
prs.body: Background and JIT enrichment could overwrite newer caller tags and metadata after PATCH. Enrichment now merges derived additions into the latest source snapshot; background relationships, derived graph fields and completion commit in one guarded graph query. Content and timestamp changes invalidate an obsolete plan, missing planned neighbors preserve the source row, and per-memory evidence accounting keeps retries from inflating temporal/pattern counters. Conditional Qdrant tag updates and nest

prs.title: fix(api): validate memory types and expose reliable diagnostics
prs.body: Admin preflight permits both supported admin headers while preserving origin/auth checks. Registered POST/PATCH/batch routes normalize known memory types, preserve custom strings with a warning, and reject blank/null/non-string types before mutation. Entity audit validation returns standard 400 responses. Structured logging emits extras safely and removes recall query text from structured events, Werkzeug access logs and vector-search DEBUG logs without mutating shared LogRecords.

prs.title: fix(test): execute service integration tests and reject skipped CI runs
prs.body: The service integration suite evaluated availability before beforeAll ran and therefore skipped every test. Probe before collection, pass explicit test credentials, use the configured vector dimension and bounded polling, and assert concrete store/recall/update/delete/relationship results. Strict runs fail if the service is unavailable or any service test is skipped or the suite is empty. A dedicated CI job provisions isolated FalkorDB/Qdrant and a pinned AutoMem fixture.

prs.body: Tool definitions now describe hierarchical tag prefixes correctly, use the canonical bugfix example, and explain that metadata updates replace the stored object. Deprecation examples preserve the complete metadata object rather than encouraging partial replacement.

prs.title: fix(recall): normalize hierarchical tag prefix filters
prs.body: Prefix filters now normalize slash and colon separators consistently across graph, vector and postfilter paths. Legacy graph nodes use hierarchy-aware fallback rather than string-prefix matching. Exact matching retains separator distinctions. Documented backfill covers existing Qdrant payloads without tag_prefixes.

prs.title: fix(embedding): retry failures and preserve vector payload state
prs.body: Async embedding jobs now retry bounded provider and Qdrant failures, reuse vectors only while their source text remains current, and expose failure/exhaustion counters in `/health.embedding`. The worker waits for Qdrant application and revalidates graph content afterward so a concurrent PATCH triggers regeneration. All seven vector writers share a payload builder preserving temporal bounds, archive state, relevance, metadata and hierarchical tag prefixes. Explicit placeholder providers continue

prs.title: fix(policy): align host tags and memory importance guidance
prs.body: Generated and hand-maintained host rules disagreed about platform/date tags and importance values. Shared guidance now covers the repository's live AGENTS.md, host rules, the primary session-start prompt and both generated Bash hooks, plugin companion examples, and both OpenClaw skills. Bugfix Insight uses importance 0.75 / confidence 0.85, articulated Pattern 0.8, and correction Preference 0.9 / 0.95. Preference examples distinguish explicit corrections and invalidate prior preferences. Hermes

prs.title: fix(runtime): preserve retries and honor Qdrant safety settings
prs.body: Strict Qdrant dimension mismatches now propagate through real collection initialization and stop default startup. Enrichment retries atomically transfer inflight protection to a pending retry, preserving bounded attempt counts and queue completion accounting. Consolidation uses the configured collection for all seven vector operations and warns on failed mutations.

prs.title: fix(recovery): preserve existing graph data during Qdrant salvage
prs.body: Qdrant recovery previously deleted the graph before fetching its source and could report success after incomplete restoration. Recovery now validates the complete source, inserts missing memories with original IDs and API-compatible properties, preserves existing nodes and relationships, and fails clearly on incomplete recovery. The monitor avoids graph salvage for a vector deficit and honors CLI > environment > defaults, including zero.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): preserve tags omitted from memory updates
prs.body: An importance-only OpenClaw update previously replaced all existing tags with the configured default project tag. Updates now omit tags unless supplied; explicit tags replace exactly, including an empty array to clear tags. Creation continues to apply defaults.

prs.title: fix(mcp-sse): preserve active legacy SSE sessions
prs.body: Legacy SSE sessions were missing access timestamps, so the abandoned-session sweep closed every connection within five minutes. Track activity and keep connected streams alive while cleaning up closed sessions.

fix(plaid): tax refunds book to income.tax_refund, not refunds received
prs.body:
## Problem
`plaidIsRefund` flags any detailed PFC ending in `_REFUND`, and Plaid's `INCOME_TAX_REFUND` matches. The categorizer's tier-4 refund shortcut (`txn.source === 'plaid' && txn.is_refund`) runs before the PFC mapping, so a tax refund lands in `income.refunds_received`, which nets against revenue on Schedule C line 1.

prs.title: fix(plaid): only real refunds take the refund shortcut
prs.body:
## Problem
`plaidIsRefund` returned true for any Plaid transaction with `transaction_type: 'special'`, whatever its sign. Plaid's deprecated `special` type also covers card autopays, transfers, ATM withdrawals and payouts, not just refunds. The categorizer's tier-4 refund shortcut runs before counterparty memory and the PFC mapping, so all of those landed in `income.refunds_received` at 0.9 confidence and reduced reported revenue in the P&L.

airflow.autojack.ai said **STALLED** on 2026-09-27 with doors open on both facades and SE wind gusting 30+ km/h. Two causes:

prs.title: fix(voice): give delegate_task a capability class so a real delegation can be spoken
prs.body:
`classifyToolName('delegate_task')` returned `'other'`, and the action-claim guard
matches `classifyToolName(entry.name) === claimClass` — so a **successful** delegation
could never license a claim naming any capability class. The model's natural
confirmation usually names one, so `runLocalNativeToolLoop`'s guard (#1549) reached
`outcome: 'gave_up'` and blanked the turn's `finalText`: a correct delegation the user
hears as silence.

fix(web): let the voice client follow the server's TTS provider
prs.body: The web voice client pinned Chatterbox. Its constructor set `provider = 'chatterbox'` and it sent `provider:set { provider: 'chatterbox' }` on every connect, a leftover from when Chatterbox was the fixed primary. Whenever Chatterbox is configured, the server honors that per-session override, so browser voice ignored `VOICE_HYBRID_TTS_PROVIDER`. With Qwen3-TTS becoming the default (#1717, owner decision 2026-09-21), the browser lane would have stayed on Chatterbox.
